newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia traders raise palm olein offer price.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia traders raise palm olein offer price.

text.p: Indonesian traders have agreed to raise their palm olein offer price to 1,500 rupiah/kg from last traded 1,460-65 rupiah, traders said on Thursday.
They said the agreement was reached at a meeting on Wednesday night in Jakarta attended by nearly all major refiners and traders.

"It's a matter of survival. There was a consensus at last night's meeting that palm olein should be offered at 1,500 rupiah because crude palm oil prices are above 1,300 rupiah/kg," one senior trader who attended the meeting told Reuters.
"The feeling was that no one should not offer below that level, but it's up to individuals," he said.
Another trader said there would be no margin in processing crude palm oil into olein at current prices. "We will be making losses if olein is not at the 1,500-rupiah level," he said.

He said the traders felt they could take the initiative now because the Moslem Eid al-Fitr festival was over and there was not expected to be any market intervention by state logistics agency BULOG to put a lid on cooking oil prices.

"During the market operations by BULOG during Eid al-Fitr, we could not do it. But now we are free," the trader said, adding that the higher crude palm oil price was due, in part, to good export prices.
Traders said nearly all players were keeping to the pact, offering olein at 1,500 rupiah on Thursday.
"One player was heard offering at 1,470-75 rupiah because he was still selling leftover BULOG oil," one trader said. "But the player is not selling in big quantities."
Traders also said the passing of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping had no impact on the market, saying the news had long been discounted in the market.
"Deng's death is not a factor," one trader said. "He has been ill and his passing was not totally unexpected."
